result.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response when sync is enabled ('return response;' from fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)), while grafted callers consume vendor-specific shapes: zoho-bigin/zohocrm use 'tokenInfo.data' and 'zohoCrmTokenInfo.data', google does 'const token = res?.data' expecting google-auth-library's result, and hubspot awaits a HubspotToken SDK object. In sync mode those properties don't exist on a fetch Response, breaking token refresh for those apps when the sync env vars are set.

judged_text: In sync mode the helper returns the raw fetch Response object, but the call sites it was grafted onto consume the response shapes of their original refresh mechanisms (axios `.data` for zoho-bigin/zohocrm, google-auth-library `.res.data` for google, the Hubspot SDK token object), so the sync path is structurally incompatible with those callers. With CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set (exactly the setup .env.example documents), google/zoho-bigin/zohocrm throw TypeErrors on every token refresh and hubspot persists undefined token fields; the credential-sync feature cannot work for these apps as shipped.
